It is approximately centered, typically around 7–10 pixels across, with a roughly one- to two-pixel outline and some variation in size, position, and roundness.

Its width, height, and position vary, mostly within rows 1–10 and columns 1–10, leaving a black outer margin. I would expect boxes several pixels wide and tall; the exact minimum and maximum dimensions are less certain.

Typical dimensions are roughly 7–10 pixels across and 6–10 pixels tall, with thin, stair-stepped sides. Some triangles may be slightly asymmetric, and grayscale edge pixels may soften the outline.

A single solid white, roughly equilateral triangle pointing up on a black background. The apex is at the top (row 1, somewhere in columns ~3–8), the sides spread about 0.6 columns per row, and the flat base lies at a variable row between about 5 and 11, so heights range from ~4 to ~10 pixels and base widths from ~4 up to the full 10 interior columns. Row 0, column 0 and column 11 are always black; the triangle is roughly centered horizontally and never touches the frame.

Each generated image is a single hollow circle: a thin (≈1 pixel wide, slightly anti‑aliased/grey at the edges) white ring on a black background. The circle's diameter is roughly 5–9 pixels (radius ≈2.5–4.5), its centre lies somewhere in the middle of the grid (roughly rows/cols 4–7), and it never touches the outer one‑pixel frame, which is always black. The interior of the ring is black.

A Pong‑style paddle game played against a wall (single‑player Pong / Breakout‑without‑bricks / squash): the agent is a paddle fixed in the left column (column 1) that moves only up and down; a ball bounces around the 8×8 court off the top, bottom and right walls.
review_rationale: Game section explicitly identifies Pong-style paddle game and single-player Pong. Breakout-without-bricks is a parenthetical analogy, not a competing game prediction; vertical paddle on left wall matches Pong.
